cues.en: Let's talk about overfitting as well.
cues.zh: 也來談談過度擬合。

cues.en: You can see you'll often end up with patterns like this, where you're not really getting a clean solution.
cues.zh: 可以看到，經常會出現這種圖樣，沒有真正得到乾淨的解。

cues.en: You end up with these weird spikes sometimes, and sometimes if you let things go a little bit too long, it ends up reinforcing those spikes, those overfitted areas where you're not really fitting
cues.zh: 有時會有奇怪尖峰；如果執行太久，最後反而強化那些尖峰、那些過度擬合的區域，不再真正擬合

cues.en: to the pattern you're looking for, you're just fitting to the training data that you were given.
cues.zh: 你要找的模式，而只是擬合給定的訓練資料。

cues.en: Obviously, if you have thousands of ways to tune, those connections between each neuron and each layer of your neurons can add up really quickly, so it's very easy for overfitting to happen.
cues.zh: 顯然，既然有數千種可調整的方式，每個神經元與每層之間的連線，很快就大量增加，因此很容易過度擬合。

cues.en: But fortunately, there are ways to deal with it.
cues.zh: 但幸好，有方法處理。

cues.en: One is called early stopping.
cues.zh: 其中一種叫做提早停止。

cues.en: So as soon as you see performance start to drop, that might be nature's way of telling you that it might be time for you to stop learning.
cues.zh: 一旦看到效能開始下降，也許就是大自然提醒你，該停止學習了。

cues.en: At this point, maybe you're just overfitting.
cues.zh: 這時，也許只是過度擬合。

cues.en: There are also regularization terms you can add to the cost function during training, which are like the bias term we talked about earlier.
cues.zh: 也能在訓練期間的成本函數加入正規化項，類似前面談過的偏差項。

cues.en: That can help too.
cues.zh: 這也有幫助。

cues.en: A surprisingly effective technique is called dropout.
cues.zh: 一種出乎意料有效的方法，叫做 Dropout。

cues.en: It's an example of a very simple idea that's very effective.
cues.zh: 這是概念簡單、卻很有效的例子。

cues.en: The idea is just to ignore, say, half of the neurons randomly at each training step.
cues.zh: 想法是，在每個訓練步驟，隨機忽略例如一半神經元。

cues.en: Pretend that they don't exist at all.
cues.zh: 假裝它們完全不存在。

cues.en: The reason this works is because it forces your model to spread out its learning.
cues.zh: 這有效，是因為強迫模型分散學習。

cues.en: If basically you're taking away half its brain at each training step, you're going to force the remaining half of those neurons to do as much work as possible.
cues.zh: 如果每個訓練步驟，都拿掉一半大腦，就會強迫剩下的一半神經元，盡可能多做事。

cues.en: This prevents things where you have individual neurons taking on more of the work than they should.
cues.zh: 避免某些神經元，承擔過多工作。

cues.en: You even saw some examples that we ran in the Tensorflow playground, where we would end up with neurons that were barely used at all, and by using dropout, that would have forced that neuron
cues.zh: TensorFlow Playground 的範例中，甚至看過有些神經元幾乎沒被使用；使用 Dropout，就會強迫那個神經元

cues.en: to have been used more effectively.
cues.zh: 更有效地被利用。

cues.en: Dropout is a very simple concept and very effective in making sure that you're making full use of your neural network, and it's also effective at combating overfitting.
cues.zh: Dropout 概念非常簡單，能有效確保充分運用神經網路，也能有效對抗過度擬合。

cues.en: Let's talk about tuning your topology.
cues.zh: 談談如何調整拓樸。

cues.en: Another way to improve the results of your deep learning network is to just play games with how many neurons you have and how many layers of neurons you have.
cues.zh: 改善深度學習網路結果的另一個方式，就是調整神經元數量與層數。

cues.en: That arrangement of neurons is what we call your topology.
cues.zh: 這種神經元的排列方式，稱為拓樸。

cues.en: One way of finding the optimal topology is just trial and error, like what we did in the Tensorflow playground.
cues.zh: 尋找最佳拓樸的一種方式，就是反覆試驗，如同 TensorFlow Playground 的做法。

cues.en: But there can be a methodology to your experiments.
cues.zh: 但實驗也可以有方法。

cues.en: You can start off with a strategy of evaluating a smaller network with less neurons in the hidden layers, or you can evaluate a larger network with more layers.
cues.zh: 可以先評估較小、隱藏層神經元較少的網路，或評估層數更多的大型網路。

cues.en: The question you're asking is, can I get away with a smaller network and still get good results?
cues.zh: 你要問的是，能否用較小網路，仍得到好結果？

cues.en: Then you just keep on making it smaller and smaller until you find the smallest it can safely be.
cues.zh: 接著，不斷縮小，直到找到仍能安全使用的最小規模。

cues.en: Or you can try to make your network larger and larger and see at what point it stops providing more benefits to you.
cues.zh: 也可以不斷加大網路，看看從哪個時候開始，不再帶來更多好處。

cues.en: In short, just start sizing things differently and see what works and what doesn't.
cues.zh: 簡單說，就是試不同規模，看看哪些有效、哪些無效。

cues.en: There's sort of a spooky aspect to how this stuff all works together.
cues.zh: 這些東西組合運作的方式，有點不可思議。

cues.en: It's very hard to understand intuitively what's going on inside of a deep neural network, so sometimes you just have to use your intuition to try to tune the thing and get at the right number of resources you need.
cues.zh: 深度神經網路內部很難直覺理解，所以有時只能靠直覺調整，找出所需的適當資源量。

cues.en: Also, in today's modern computing environments, sometimes you don't really care so much.
cues.zh: 另外，在現代運算環境，有時不必那麼在意。

cues.en: It's probably okay to have a deep neural network that has a few more neurons than it really needs.
cues.zh: 神經網路比實際需要多幾個神經元，可能也沒關係。

cues.en: I mean, what's the real expense involved in that these days?
cues.zh: 以現在來說，真正多花多少成本？

cues.en: Probably not much, unless your data is truly massive, like YouTube or something.
cues.zh: 可能不多，除非資料像 YouTube 那樣龐大。

cues.en: In general, however, more layers will often yield faster learning than having more neurons in less layers.
cues.zh: 不過，一般而言，增加層數，通常比在較少層中增加神經元，學得更快。

cues.en: If you care about speed of convergence, adding more layers is often the right thing to do.
cues.zh: 如果在意收斂速度，增加層數通常是正確做法。

cues.en: You can also use something called model zoos.
cues.zh: 也可以使用所謂的模型動物園，也就是 Model Zoo。

cues.en: There are actually libraries out there of neural network topologies for specific problems.
cues.zh: 其實已經有針對特定問題的神經網路拓樸函式庫。

cues.en: If you don't think you're the first person in the world to solve a specific problem with a deep neural network, maybe you should check out one of the model zoos out there
cues.zh: 如果不認為自己是世上第一個用深度神經網路解決特定問題的人，也許該看看這些模型動物園，

cues.en: to see if someone's already figured out the optimal topology for what you're trying to achieve, instead of trying to reinvent the wheel.
cues.zh: 是否已有人找出適合你目標的最佳拓樸，而不是重新發明輪子。

cues.en: People share these things for a reason, and it can save you a lot of time.
cues.zh: 人們分享這些東西是有原因的，能替你省下很多時間。

cues.en: Enough theory.
cues.zh: 理論夠了。

cues.en: In our next lecture, we'll get our hands dirty with Tensorflow and start writing some real Python code to implement our own neural networks.
cues.zh: 下一堂會實作 TensorFlow，開始寫真正的 Python 程式碼，建立自己的神經網路。
